proposed_comments.title: Initialize WinRT before BugReportTool uses it

confidence.rationale: Exact-head source shows no apartment initialization in wmain, the production sanitizer invokes WinRT JSON, and the test fixture initializes an apartment explicitly.

proposed_comments.body:
### Initialize WinRT before BugReportTool uses it

**Severity:** `medium`

**Affected code:** `wmain`, `ReportWindowsSettings`, and the `diagnostic_privacy::sanitize_report` call in `tools/BugReportTool/BugReportTool/Main.cpp`.

**Problem:** `wmain` does not initialize a WinRT apartment, yet `ReportWindowsSettings` calls WinRT globalization APIs and the new sanitizer invokes WinRT JSON parsing. The former catches and hides failures; the sanitizer's outer catch deletes the report directory and returns failure.

**Why it matters:** A missing apartment can turn the new privacy pass into a hard failure that prevents the bug-report ZIP from being produced.

**Suggested change:** Initialize a WinRT apartment at the beginning of `wmain`, before any WinRT caller, and pair it with scope-bound `winrt::uninit_apartment()`.

**Verification:** At `0378389`, the exact source shows `ReportWindowsSettings` before `sanitize_report`, no `init_apartment` in `wmain`, and `JsonValue::TryParse` in the sanitizer. The privacy-test fixture explicitly initializes WinRT before exercising that code; no production-entry-point test covers the missing initialization.

proposed_comments.title: Terminate and reap the extractor on timeout

confidence.rationale: The exact-head helper launches tar.exe and asserts the 30-second wait result without a timeout cleanup path.

proposed_comments.body:
### Terminate and reap the extractor on timeout

**Severity:** `low`

**Affected code:** `DiagnosticPrivacyTests.cpp`'s `ExtractArchive` helper at the 30-second `WaitForSingleObject` call.

**Problem:** If the wait returns `WAIT_TIMEOUT`, the immediately following assertion fails without terminating or waiting for the launched `tar.exe` process.

**Why it matters:** A timed-out extractor can continue running after its test fails and keep using the temporary archive or directory while later tests proceed.

**Suggested change:** Save the wait result; on `WAIT_TIMEOUT`, terminate the child and wait until it is signaled before asserting. Read its exit code only after `WAIT_OBJECT_0`.

**Verification:** At exact head `0378389`, `ExtractArchive` launches `tar.exe` and asserts the 30-second wait result at line 803; the timeout path has no termination or reaping. The normal extraction test does not exercise a hung child.

proposed_comments.title: Preserve the cause when report sanitization fails

confidence.rationale: The exact-head sanitizer uses throwing file streams and WinRT parsing, while the new outer catch discards all error details.

proposed_comments.body:
### Preserve the cause when report sanitization fails

**Severity:** `low`

**Affected code:** The catch-all around `diagnostic_privacy::sanitize_report` in `tools/BugReportTool/BugReportTool/Main.cpp`.

**Problem:** Any exception from WinRT parsing or file access is discarded, and the tool prints the same generic message before deleting the report directory.

**Why it matters:** When no ZIP is created, users and maintainers cannot distinguish a file-access failure from a WinRT or parsing failure, making the failure harder to diagnose.

**Suggested change:** Preserve a sanitized error category or HRESULT for known WinRT/filesystem failures, retain a generic fallback for unknown exceptions, and keep the existing cleanup and failure return. Avoid logging report contents or sensitive paths.

**Verification:** At exact head `0378389`, the sanitizer configures its input/output streams to throw and invokes WinRT JSON parsing; the `Main.cpp` catch-all erases the exception type and reports only the same generic message. No runtime failure was triggered for this assessment.
